primary_inspected.citation: Hughes JM, Schindler M, Francis CA (2005). The C2/m disordered structure of pascoite, Ca3[V10O28]·17H2O: bonding between structural units and interstitial complexes in compounds containing the [V10O28]6− decavanadate polyanion. Canadian Mineralogist 43:1379–1386.
primary_inspected.coverage: Complete eight-page original and all printed figures/tables inspected in prior same-day handoff; unchanged PDF bytes rechecked and methods, structural model, figures and table limits reread in round102. Official thermal-parameter DOCX and FCF deposits freshly acquired and inspected in round102.

locators.specimen_and_methods: p. 1380; Harvard specimen 91449, Minasragra, Peru; Table 1
locators.deposits: Article p1380 calls deposits Tables 4/5; official MAC index and downloaded files label thermal parameters Table5 and FCF Table6. Printed article Table5 is a separate comparative table.

supported: Natural museum-specimen single-crystal refinement supports a disordered C2/m structure built from decavanadate units and hydrated calcium complexes.
The Ca1 water disorder allows differing local coordination; its average coordination must not be represented as a unique fixed environment.
Hydrogen positions were constrained during refinement; the paper does not provide an unconstrained neutron determination.
limits: This is not a bulk-ore assay, microbial mechanism, controlled extraction, or industrial deployment experiment.
Comparison residuals for non-hydrogen-only models must not be conflated with the final hydrogen-containing refinement residual.
Printed cross-compound structural comparisons do not establish controlled pascoite dehydration kinetics.

primary_inspected.citation: Weeks AD, Thompson ME, Sherwood AM (1955). Navajoite, a new vanadium oxide from Arizona. American Mineralogist 40:207–212.
primary_inspected.coverage: Complete six-page original text and rendered pages; chemistry pages enlarged independently of OCR.

locators.occurrence: pp. 207–209, Monument No. 2 mine, Apache County, Arizona

supported: A relatively pure selected natural specimen was characterized chemically and by diffraction, with residual impurity and substitution alternatives retained.
The original water-rich formula and tentative indexing are historical interpretations, superseded by the later reassessment and current IMA row.
limits: Bulk V2O4 may reflect reduced vanadium or an admixed phase; authors argued against a large corvusite admixture without proving complete phase purity.
Storage-related water loss lacks controlled humidity and a kinetic protocol. Natural oxidation of corvusite was an interpretation, not a controlled transformation or microbial experiment.
Do not substitute the tentative original V2O5·3H2O formula for the current IMA species formula.
primary_inspected.license: unknown article-specific redistribution license; USGS authorship does not by itself license the journal copy

primary_inspected.citation: Evans HT Jr, Hughes JM (1990). Crystal chemistry of the natural vanadium bronzes. American Mineralogist 75:508–521.
primary_inspected.coverage: Complete 14-page original, all rendered figures/tables, with focused enlarged navajoite discussion and Table 7.

locators.specimen_reidentification: pp. 517–519, including Table 6 and navajoite section

supported: New powder/fiber diffraction reindexes USNM 106900, whose type status is explicitly uncertain; some extra lines were attributed to probable bokite.
The current formula is informed by reinterpretation of the original 1955 chemical analysis, not a newly independent chemical assay.
Some material labeled navajoite proved to be bokite or mixtures; specimens discussed in other mineral sections must not be transferred to this species.
limits: C2/m unit-cell indexing is not a solved atomic structure. The article explicitly leaves the structural principle unknown.
The fitted empirical formula Ca0.05(V9.48Fe0.52)Σ10O24·12H2O must not be silently promoted to the ideal IMA formula.
Ross 1959 electron-diffraction results are discussed secondhand; the Ross original was not acquired in this bounded task.
